newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds rise more on S&P company upgrades.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds rise more on S&P company upgrades.

text.p: Argentine bonds were higher late morning Wednesday, boosted by news of upgrades to several Argentine banks and corporations by Standard & Poor's Tuesday.
"The upgrades gave the market impetus," said a trader at a local bank.
Corporate Eurobonds and Argentine Brady bonds were higher in London on the upgrades and that in turn carried through to the local market, said traders.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 was up 1/2 at 90-3/4, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 rose $0.25 to 125.95.
Declines in the U.S. 30-year Treasury yield Tuesday helped the market, said traders.
Another trader said performance through the session will depend in part on the outcome of the U.S. five-year note auction, the results of which will be out later in the afternoon.
